title: Arithmetic classification and non-Pisot singularity for Bernoulli convolutions
main_claim: (1) For every λ∈(0,1), ν_λ is singular iff λ lies in an explicit set C defined by one-sided 4^{-n}-approximation by retained height-one algebraic units of degree dn (mod-2 irreducible minimal polynomials) whose nearby units supply many distinct initial coefficient vectors in at least a 1/d fraction of orthants. (2) ν_{1/β} is singular for every quartic Salem number β∈(1,2). (3) ν_{1/β} is singular for the non-Pisot real root β≈1.8392867573 of p(t)=t^31−2t^30+Σ_{j=0}^{9}(t^{3j+1}−t^{3j}). This polynomial has a conjugate pair with |α|^2≈1.000209.

issues.location: nonpisot.tex, proof of Prop. np:typical-gain (coupling paragraph)
issues.description: The coupling claims the finite and stationary truncated characters agree for H+2000 ≤ i ≤ N−1−H. But the type-1 predictor term Z^{(1)}_{i-33} involves Z_{i-36}, and C_1 shifts C_0 by +3 and −1, so the lower threshold should be about H+2036. Only an O(H) number of boundary indices is affected, so the conclusion is unchanged.
issues.evidence: Z^{(1)}_{i-33}=Z_{i-36}·conj(Z_{i-33})·Z_{i-32}; the predictor uses k up to 2000.

Also ran a high-precision mpmath check for β root of x^4−x^3−x^2−x+1 with k=(62),(62,2491): S=41.4→80.6 (≈doubling), L=6.0→13.3, the positive-index sum matches S, and the minimum |cos| is preserved, all consistent with Lemmas sal:construction and sal:loss.
